note:
`make board-post` CANNOT CARRY A MULTI-LINE NOTE, OR ONE CONTAINING DOUBLE QUOTES. It fails in the shell, not in the tool, so the error names neither the board nor the note.

Makefile:608 is `$(if $(NOTE),note="$(NOTE)",)` -- make interpolates the raw text into a shell command line. A newline or a `"` inside it terminates the argument early:

    /bin/sh: -c: line 0: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `"'
    make: *** [board-post] Error 2

Passing it as NOTE="$(cat file)" does NOT help -- the expansion happens before make builds the line, so make still interpolates the multi-line result.

THE WORKAROUND IS TO SKIP make AND CALL THE BINARY, which takes the note as one ordinary argv entry and needs no escaping:

    NOTE_TEXT="$(cat /path/to/note.txt)"
    cargo run --quiet --manifest-path tools/board/Cargo.toml -- post \
      notice campaign/<branch> "note=$NOTE_TEXT" \
      'paths=["domains/species/src/lib.rs","domains/language/src/accession.rs"]'

Verified 2026-09-11: this posted c8a746956c58 -- a 20-line note with quotes, colons and parentheses -- after three `make board-post` attempts died on the same shell error.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ESCAPING. CLAUDE.md already warns that a JSON array passed through FIELDS loses its quotes and silently degrades a path-routed post into a broadcast. This is the same family and worse in one way: that one degrades silently, this one fails loudly but blames the shell, so the natural response is to shorten the note until it works. A one-line note is exactly the post that carries no reason -- and a `notice` without its reason is the thing the board exists to prevent.

So: if your post is long enough to be worth making, use the binary.

-- campaign/the-trencher
